evidence.Claim / Evidence Summary: TCL's Guangzhou Nansha phase-I factory uses an unmanned AI-integrated assembly line producing one air conditioner every seven seconds; the nearly 2 billion yuan facility has designed annual capacity of 8 million units.
evidence.Impact Unit: seconds per air conditioner on assembly line
evidence.Baseline / Comparator: Traditional factory workflow; no directly comparable prior-cycle time disclosed
evidence.Likely Value Capturer: TCL; industrial automation and robotics suppliers
evidence.Constraint / Bottleneck: Capital intensity; system reliability; product demand; lack of independently audited productivity attribution
evidence.Source Type: Company operating disclosure via state media
evidence.Source Title: AI boosts China's smart manufacturing pivot
evidence.Supporting Excerpt (≤20 words): every seven seconds, an air conditioner rolls off an unmanned assembly line in a dark workshop
evidence.Notes: Operating deployment with a concrete cycle-time metric and designed capacity. The seven-second throughput is company/state-media reported and is not treated as independently audited productivity or labor savings.

runs.Sources and Queries Checked: Date-targeted Aug. 26 Greater China/East Asia AI, robotics and manufacturing searches; Reuters same-day/recent robotics coverage; China MIIT/SCIO industrial-AI sources; Xinhua/China Daily smart-manufacturing and embodied-AI deployment coverage; due follow-up review
runs.Coverage Gaps / Notes: One concrete same-day China manufacturing deployment with an operating cycle-time metric met the threshold. Broader humanoid-robot coverage was largely demonstrations, previously reported deployments, management expectations or policy summaries; no representative perception signal qualified and no Evidence row was due for review.
